title: Design a Web Crawler
prompt: Design a web crawler that starts from a set of seed URLs, discovers and fetches pages, extracts links, and continues crawling — at large scale, and politely (respecting each site's crawl rate).
requirements: Functional: fetch a page, parse out links, enqueue new URLs, avoid re-crawling the same page unnecessarily
Non-functional: billions of pages, must not overwhelm any single site (politeness/rate limiting per domain), should be resumable after a crash
discussion_points: URL frontier design: prioritization and per-domain politeness/rate limiting
Duplicate URL and duplicate-content detection at this scale
Distributing crawling work across many worker machines
DNS resolution and fetch performance at scale
Storage for the URL frontier and crawled content
Handling crawler traps (infinite URL spaces) and malformed pages
